scores.tell: Cup glaze is slightly more uniformly glossy than the matte-leaning real cards. Otherwise smooth, soft, and consistent with the real set.
Truss and housing are smooth, uniformly satin plastic with little matte/gloss variation. Fairly close to the real cards but a bit generic.
Wood faces are very smooth and soft-blurred, with fine grain streaks and little highlight variation. Hinges are plain. It looks slightly airbrushed and the floor is flat.
Painterly smeared airbrush on the wings, clouds and fuselage. Soft blurry marks with no crisp material edges. Looks like a different, illustrated style.
Glossy red paint and glass panes are broadly plausible. Slight over-lacquer on the booth. The crown and phone are chunky and the surfaces are even.
Stone pedestals have faint vein scratches. The grass is flat and illustrated, and the chess board is tiny and crisp. It reads as a flat painted illustration, not the real cards' soft 3D finish.
Leather has a smooth satin sheen with soft highlights. It has no stitching and the stirrups are a little glossy. Very close to the grade-5 saddle.
Chunky smooth plastic with soft highlights. Matte and gloss are reasonably varied, and the truss detail is simplified. Fits the real cards.
Duck body is uniformly glossy rubber-toy plastic. The spring and bolts are fine, but the sand grain is noisy and the gloss range is narrow.
Teal body is strongly glossy with broad reflection streaks. The bezels and buttons are uniformly shiny with a bit of a toy-plastic feel. It has little matte contrast.
